Functionality: F01 Translate a verbal story into events / random variables
Recognition clues: Any word problem; 'what is the probability that…'; several interacting objects
Required output: A named event or RV with an explicit verbal definition ('Let A = …', 'Let X = number of …')
Main method: Name every object before computing. Prefer defining an RV over building Ω explicitly
Common traps: Defining X ambiguously (e.g. 'number of draws' - including or excluding the last draw?); silently switching definitions between subparts
Exam sources: EVERY open question. 2023spA Q1a; 2024wB Q3c; 2021spB Q5a

Functionality: F02 Choose an appropriate probability model (equally-likely vs. constructed)
Recognition clues: 'chosen at random', 'each arrangement equally likely', 'uniformly'
Required output: Either |A|/|Ω| with both sets described, or an arithmetic route with no explicit Ω
Main method: Equally-likely space when finite and symmetric; otherwise multiplication rule / total probability
Common traps: Mixing an ordered numerator with an unordered denominator; assuming uniformity that is not stated
Current-course sources: T0 combinatorics; T1; Raviv §1.1 remark 'ordered vs unordered'
Exam sources: 2023spB Q1a-c (rooks, explicitly shows both ordered and unordered routes); 2024wA Q1b (three equivalent routes); 2017spB Q1

Functionality: F03 Rewrite an event using a complement
Recognition clues: 'at least one', 'not all', 'some row/column contains…'
Required output: P(A) = 1 - P(A^c) with A^c described verbally
Main method: Complement + independence, or complement + inclusion-exclusion
Common traps: Forgetting that 'not all identical' is not the same as 'all different'; complementing inside a conditional by mistake
Current-course sources: T1 Q on inclusion-exclusion; Raviv §1.2 example (Alsace wineries)
Exam sources: 2024wA Q1b (P(B)=1-P(B^c)); 2024wB Q4c; 2022spC Q1; Raviv §1.2 ex.2

Functionality: F04 Inclusion-exclusion (2 sets, n sets, with symmetry)
Recognition clues: Union of several overlapping events; 'at least one of…'
Required output: Numeric probability or a closed-form sum
Main method: P(∪A_i) = Σ - Σ + …; use symmetry to collapse to binomial coefficients times a common term
Common traps: Losing the alternating sign; forgetting the C(n,k) multiplicity when using symmetry
Exam sources: 2022spC Q10 (expressing 'exactly 2 of 3'); 2019spA Q1 (divisible by 2, not by 3, not by 8)

Functionality: F05 Decide what to condition on
Recognition clues: A two-stage experiment; 'first … then …'; a parameter that is itself random
Required output: A clean statement 'condition on X = x' followed by a tractable conditional law
Main method: Condition on the quantity that makes the rest independent / classical
Common traps: Conditioning on something that does not simplify; conditioning on a zero-probability event without using densities
Exam sources: 2023spA Q3 (condition on U); 2024wB Q4 (condition on N); 2021spA Q4; 2019spB Q5

Functionality: F06 Law of total probability (discrete and continuous versions)
Recognition clues: 'The rate itself is random'; 'first draw N, then…'
Required output: P(A) = Σ P(A|B_n)P(B_n) or ∫ P(A|U=u) f_U(u) du
Main method: Partition Ω; verify the partition covers everything
Common traps: Using the discrete formula where the conditioning variable is continuous; partition not exhaustive
Exam sources: 2023spA Q3c (∫ version); 2024wB Q4c; 2021spA Q2 (continuous analogue); 2021spB Q5c
Revision note: PROMOTED: now the only route to results previously reachable by quoting Poisson splitting

Functionality: F07 Bayes' rule - discrete
Recognition clues: 'Given that the result was positive/won/…, what is the probability that…'
Required output: A posterior probability
Main method: Bayes with total probability in the denominator
Common traps: Inverting the conditioning direction; forgetting the denominator's full partition
Exam sources: 2020spA-sol Q6 (covid test); 2018wB Q6 (mad-goat disease); 2020spB-sol Q4'; 2018wA Q16

Functionality: F08 Continuous Bayes / density of a parameter given an event
Recognition clues: 'Find f_{U | T>t}(u)'; 'the conditional density of X given …'
Required output: A density in u, correctly normalised
Main method: f_{U|A}(u) = P(A|U=u) f_U(u) / P(A)
Common traps: Leaving the answer unnormalised; forgetting the support restriction imposed by A
Exam sources: 2023spA Q3e (EXACT template); 2019spB Q11; 2021spB Q2 (Gamma via Bayes)
Revision note: PROMOTED to top-5: carried by 2023spA Q3e and 2023spB Q4c

Functionality: F09 Multiplication (chain) rule for sequential draws
Recognition clues: Drawing without replacement; a colour/state that changes after each draw
Required output: A product of conditional probabilities
Common traps: Using the same probability at every step when the urn composition changes
Exam sources: 2024wB Q3c (balls repainted white); 2023spB Q1; 6637-sol ת'Q1 (urn R red / B blue)

Functionality: F10 Symmetry / exchangeability shortcut
Recognition clues: 'the k-th ball drawn', 'a specific card', 'the first rook'
Required output: A one-line answer justified by symmetry, plus a combinatorial cross-check
Main method: Argue all positions are exchangeable, so P(k-th) = P(1st)
Common traps: Claiming symmetry when the objects are NOT exchangeable (e.g. after conditioning on an asymmetric event)
Exam sources: 2023spB Q3a (ace of hearts with North - 'can also be obtained directly by symmetry'); 2024wA Q1d (E(X0)=E(X1) by symmetry); 6637-sol ת'Q1b

Functionality: F11 Bernoulli-trial recognition and the four derived distributions
Recognition clues: 'independent repeated trials'; 'until the first success'; 'exactly k successes'
Required output: Bin / Geo / NegBin / Multinomial with explicit parameters
Main method: Wrap the outcome as success/failure; check p is the same each trial
Common traps: Geometric off-by-one (counting the successful trial or not); using Bin when sampling is without replacement (should be HG)
Exam sources: 2023spA Q1c (Geo(3/4)); 2024wB Q3e (sum of geometrics); 2019spB Q6; 2018wA Q1

Functionality: F12 Hypergeometric recognition
Recognition clues: 'without replacement', 'a hand of 13 cards', 'k of the n chosen items are special'
Required output: HG(N,G,n) with parameters named
Main method: Count 'good' items among a sample drawn without replacement
Common traps: Using Bin instead of HG; mislabelling which of N,G,n is which
Exam sources: 2023spB Q3b-e (explicit HG route); 2024wA Q1a-c (HG route offered as 'דרך ב'); 2019spA Q13

Functionality: F13 Memorylessness (geometric and exponential)
Recognition clues: 'given that it has already lasted more than t'; 'given at least k throws'
Required output: E(X | X ≥ k) = (k-1) + E(X), or P(X>t+s|X>s)=P(X>t)
Main method: Quote the memoryless property and shift
Common traps: Applying it to a non-memoryless law; forgetting the shift constant

Functionality: F14 Indicator method for expectation
Recognition clues: 'expected number of …' where the objects are similar but possibly dependent
Required output: E(X)=Σ E(I_k)=Σ P(A_k)
Main method: Write X as a sum of indicators; use linearity (independence NOT required)
Common traps: Trying to find the distribution of X first; assuming independence unnecessarily
Exam sources: 2023spA Q2b; 2023spB Q1d; 2024wA Q1d; 2021spA Q7a; 2020spB-sol Q5; 8598-sol Q12

Functionality: F15 Variance of a sum of DEPENDENT indicators
Recognition clues: 'variance of the number of …' after an indicator-based expectation
Required output: Var(X)=Σ Var(I_k) + Σ_{k≠j} Cov(I_k,I_j), with Cov computed from P(A_k ∩ A_j)
Main method: E(I_k I_j)=P(A_k ∩ A_j); enumerate the overlap cases
Common traps: Assuming independence and dropping the covariance terms; miscounting how many ordered pairs (k,j) fall in each overlap class
Exam sources: 2023spA Q2c; 2023spB Q1e; 2024wA Q1e (three overlap classes: same cell / same row / disjoint); 2021spA Q7b; 6637-sol ת'Q3 (coins in a circle - adjacent overlap)

Functionality: F16 Find a normalisation constant
Recognition clues: 'for an appropriate constant c'; density given up to a constant
Required output: c such that the integral over the support equals 1
Main method: Integrate over the drawn support; solve for c
Common traps: Integrating over the wrong support; forgetting the Jacobian if you substituted
Exam sources: 2020spA-sol Q12 (f = c e^{-(ax+by)}); 2018wA Q2; 8598-sol Q5

Functionality: F17 Find a CDF, then differentiate to get a density
Recognition clues: 'find the density of Y = g(X)'; a min/max; a mod-1 wrap; a piecewise definition
Required output: F_Y(y) then f_Y(y)=F_Y'(y), with the support stated
Main method: Always go via {Y ≤ y} rewritten as an event about X
Common traps: Differentiating before restricting to the support; forgetting |dx/dy| when doing a direct change of variables; missing the flat pieces of F
Current-course sources: T8; T9; T11 (8 transformation items); Raviv §5, §13, §13.4
Exam sources: 2024wB Q2b-e (density of U+V, U-V, (U+V) mod 1, (W+V) mod 1); 2018wA Q7; 2018wB Q10; 2021spA Q6a

Functionality: F18 Draw the support of a joint distribution
Recognition clues: f_{X,Y} given with a constraint like 0<x<y<∞, |x|<y, or 'uniform on a triangle'
Required output: A labelled sketch of the region in the (x,y) plane
Main method: Sketch first, integrate second
Common traps: Integrating x from 0 to ∞ when x<y binds; not noticing the region is a triangle with a sloped edge
Exam sources: 2020spB-sol Q2 (0<x<y<∞); c2adcfa6 Q1 (uniform on a triangle - solution explicitly says 'it is recommended to sketch the triangle'); 2018wA Q3; 2022spC Q6

Functionality: F19 Determine and split double-integral limits
Recognition clues: Computing P(2X<Y), P(X≤0.5, Y>1), or a marginal from a joint density
Required output: Correct inner/outer limits, split into cases if the region changes
Main method: Fix the outer variable, read the inner range off the sketch
Common traps: Constant limits where they should depend on the other variable; not splitting when min/max switches branch
Exam sources: 2020spA-sol Q12 (P(2X<Y)); 2020spB-sol Q6 (f_Z(b) with min/max limits); 2022spC Q8

Functionality: F20 Marginal distribution from a joint (discrete and continuous)
Recognition clues: 'find f_Y(y)' / 'find p_X(x)' when the joint is given
Required output: A density/PMF with support
Main method: Integrate/sum out the other variable over the correct range
Common traps: Integrating over the full line instead of the support
Exam sources: 2020spB-sol Q2 (marginal of X is Gamma(2,2)); 2022spC Q6; 8598-sol Q5
Revision note: PROMOTED from Critical-tier-2: the marginal-by-integration step is now the main route in the replacement Core question 2023spB Q4b

Functionality: F21 Conditional distribution of one RV given another
Recognition clues: 'the conditional distribution of Y given X=x is …' or 'find f_{Y|X}'
Required output: f_{Y|X}(y|x)=f_{X,Y}(x,y)/f_X(x), with the x-dependent support
Main method: Divide by the marginal; keep the support conditional on x
Common traps: Forgetting the support depends on x; treating f_{Y|X} as a function of x when normalising
Exam sources: 2023spA Q3 (T|U=u ~ Exp(u)); 2020spA-sol Q3 (Y|X=x ~ U(ax,bx)); 2020spB-sol Q2 ('from uniqueness of the density we immediately get Y|X=x ~ Uni(0,x)')

Functionality: F22 Recognise a known conditional structure inside a joint density
Recognition clues: A joint density that factorises as f_X(x)·f_{Y|X}(y|x) with both factors standard
Required output: 'X ~ Gamma(2,2) and Y|X=x ~ Uni(0,x)' - stated, not integrated
Main method: Pattern-match the joint against known density formulas
Common traps: Grinding out the integrals when pattern-matching is immediate; missing that the Gamma kernel is hiding a factor of x
Exam sources: 2020spB-sol Q2 ('כמו שראינו בתרגול, מיחידות של פונקציית הצפיפות נקבל מיידית'); 2018wA Q14
Revision note: Gamma remains examinable; ONLY the Poisson-Gamma relationship is excluded, and this functionality does not use it

Functionality: F23 Test independence of random variables
Recognition clues: 'are X and Y independent? prove your answer'
Required output: A proof: either factorisation for ALL (x,y), or one counterexample pair
Main method: f_{X,Y}=f_X f_Y AND rectangular support; or p(x,y)=p(x)p(y) for all pairs
Common traps: Concluding independence from Cov=0; ignoring a non-rectangular support (which alone kills independence)
Exam sources: 2021spB Q7c (are X and Y independent? prove); 2021spA Q5a (prove X2 and X3-X2 independent); 2024wB Q1e

Functionality: F24 Distribution of a transformation of one RV
Recognition clues: Y = X^3, Y = e^X, Y = floor(X), Y = 1 - 0.5√(4-X²)
Required output: PMF/density/CDF of Y
Main method: CDF method (F17); or monotone change of variables with |dx/dy|
Common traps: Non-monotone g (must split the domain); forgetting absolute value of the derivative
Exam sources: 2018wA Q7 (piecewise X³/X²); 2018wB Q10; 2020spA-sol Q8 (Y=min(⌊X⌋,b))
Revision note: PROMOTED: was covered only by an Extra item; now explicitly in the Extra set as mandatory

Functionality: F25 Sum of independent RVs / convolution
Recognition clues: Z = X + Y with X,Y independent
Required output: Density of Z, possibly piecewise
Main method: f_Z(z)=∫ f_X(x) f_Y(z-x) dx; watch both indicator constraints
Common traps: Not intersecting the two supports, giving a density that is not piecewise; forgetting to check ∫f_Z = 1
Exam sources: 2024wB Q2b (U+V); 2020spB-sol Q6; 2018wA Q10 (X-Y for exponentials); 8598-sol Q6

Functionality: F26 Sums of independent normals / linear combinations
Recognition clues: Several independent N(0,1) weights summed along a path
Required output: A named normal with computed mean and variance
Main method: Sum of independent normals is normal; Var adds
Common traps: Adding standard deviations instead of variances; forgetting cross-covariances when the summands share terms
Exam sources: 2023spA Q4a,b,e (tree with N(0,1) edge weights); 2019spB Q15 (SAME tree skeleton with Exp weights); 8598-sol Q16
Revision note: Sums/linear combinations of independent normals remain examinable. The claim "a linear image of a normal VECTOR is jointly normal", and writing a 2x2 covariance matrix, are EXCLUDED (multivariate normal)

Functionality: F27 Covariance and correlation coefficient
Recognition clues: 'find Cov(X,Y)' / 'find ρ'
Required output: A number or formula; ρ ∈ [-1,1]
Main method: Cov(X,Y)=E(XY)-E(X)E(Y); bilinearity for sums; ρ=Cov/(σ_X σ_Y)
Common traps: Forgetting bilinearity lets you split a covariance of two sums into shared terms only; sign errors
Exam sources: 2023spA Q4c (Cov = 3 - d/2); 2021spA Q5c (ρ(X2,X3)); 2021spB Q4 (ρ via Poisson splitting); 2018wA Q3

Functionality: F28 Conditional expectation and the tower (smoothing) law
Recognition clues: 'first draw N, then…'; E(X) where X depends on a random parameter
Required output: E(X)=E(E(X|Y))
Main method: Compute E(X|Y=y) as a function of y, then take expectation over Y
Common traps: Treating E(X|Y) as a number instead of a random function of Y; forgetting to average
Exam sources: 2023spA Q3b; 2024wA Q4a; 2024wB Q4b; 2022spC Q4; 2021spA Q6c; 2020spB-sol Q1

Functionality: F29 Conditional variance and the EVE law
Recognition clues: Variance of a two-stage quantity
Required output: Var(X)=E(Var(X|Y))+Var(E(X|Y))
Main method: Compute both pieces separately
Common traps: Dropping the second term; computing Var(E(X|Y)) as E(Var(...))
Exam sources: Weakly represented in the exams in this folder - see 09 route, 'poorly represented topics'
Revision note: PROMOTED from Moderate: with MGFs and Poisson processes removed, conditional variance is now one of the few examinable topics with no exam precedent, which raises rather than lowers its expected value

Functionality: F30 Wald / sum of a random number of independent RVs
Recognition clues: S = X_1 + … + X_N with N random and independent of the X_i
Required output: E(S)=E(N)E(X_1); distribution via total probability or MGF
Main method: Wald's identity, or tower law
Common traps: Using Wald when N is NOT independent of the X_i; using it for variance (needs the full formula)
Exam sources: 2024wA Q4a ('לפי נוסחת וואלד' and the tower-law alternative); 2017spB Q7; 2019spA Q7
Revision note: DOWNGRADED from Critical: its best specimen (2024wA Q4a) now sits inside an otherwise excluded question, so coverage is thin. Still a named syllabus topic (item 18)

Functionality: F31 Poisson splitting / thinning
Recognition clues: N ~ Pois(λ); each of the N items is independently 'type A' with probability p
Required output: The type-A count ~ Pois(λp), and the type counts are INDEPENDENT
Main method: Quote splitting; or derive via total probability with Bin(n,p) inside
Common traps: Forgetting that the split parts are independent (this is the whole point); using it when N is not Poisson
Exam sources: 2024wA Q4b,c (both the one-line splitting route and the full derivation); 2024wB Q4b,c; 2021spB Q4 ('פיצול פואסון'); 2017spB Q5 (cars turning at a junction)
Revision note: Poisson processes are officially excluded. Retained in the historical inventory only

Functionality: F32 Moment generating functions - identify a distribution from its MGF
Recognition clues: 'X has MGF M_X(t) = …'; 'find P(X=0)'
Required output: The name and parameters of X, then the requested quantity
Main method: Compare with the MGF table; use M_{X+b}(t)=e^{bt}M_X(t) and M_{aX}(t)=M_X(at); products mean independent sums
Common traps: Forgetting that a product of MGFs = sum of independent RVs, and a convex combination of MGFs = a mixture; algebra slips with e^t
Current-course sources: Raviv §9.8.1 (NOT covered in the Spring-2026 tutorials - self-study)
Exam sources: 2021spA Q4 (mixture of two Poisson MGFs); 2019spA Q10; 2019spB Q5; 2020spB-sol Q1'; 2020spA-sol Q10; 8598-sol Q9
Revision note: Moment generating functions are officially excluded. Retained in the historical inventory only

Functionality: F33 Maxima, minima and order statistics via the CDF
Recognition clues: 'the largest/smallest of n independent…'; X_(k)
Required output: P(max ≤ x) = F(x)^n; P(min > x) = (1-F(x))^n; then the joint or the PMF
Main method: Always go through the CDF, never guess the density
Common traps: Using max/min formulas without independence; forgetting P(min>y) needs the strict complement; sign slips when converting a joint CDF into a joint PMF
Current-course sources: T9; Raviv §5 (technique appears; no dedicated section)
Exam sources: 2024wB Q1 (full 5-part development of max and min of n dice, ending in the joint PMF); 2019spA Q9,Q11; 2018wA Q4,Q5; 2020spB-sol Q3; 2022spC Q8

Functionality: F34 Markov's inequality
Recognition clues: 'bound from above the probability that…'; only the mean is known
Required output: P(X ≥ a) ≤ E(X)/a for X ≥ 0
Main method: Make the RV non-negative first (often by taking |·|^n)
Common traps: Applying it to an RV that can be negative; a bound bigger than 1 (useless but not wrong)
Exam sources: 2024wA Q2e (P(|X-E X|>x) ≤ C_n/x^n via Markov on |X-EX|^n - EXCELLENT); 2021spB Q6d

Functionality: F35 Chebyshev's inequality
Recognition clues: 'bound the probability of deviating from the mean'; variance is known or computable
Required output: P(|X-μ|≥ε) ≤ σ²/ε²
Main method: Compute Var first, then substitute
Common traps: Using ε as a fraction rather than an absolute deviation; forgetting the two-sided factor
Current-course sources: T12 (Chebyshev ×11 - the most drilled item in T12); Raviv §10.3
Exam sources: 2023spB Q2d (explicitly notes the bound exceeds 1 and is therefore useless - a deliberate trap); 2023spA Q2e; 2021spB Q6

Functionality: F36 Convergence in probability (weak law) proved by hand
Recognition clues: 'show that X_n converges weakly / in probability to L'; a reminder of the definition is given
Required output: lim P(|X_n - L|>ε)=0, proved
Main method: Triangle inequality to split |X_n - L| ≤ |X_n - E X_n| + |E X_n - L|, then Chebyshev on the first part and a limit on the second
Common traps: Applying Chebyshev directly to |X_n - L| when E X_n ≠ L; forgetting that Var → 0 is what does the work
Exam sources: 2023spA Q2e (full template with the triangle-inequality split); 2023spB Q2e (two routes: continuity+WLLN, or Chebyshev); 2021spA Q6d; 2021spA Q7c
Revision note: Convergence IN PROBABILITY (weak) is examinable. ALMOST-SURE convergence and the strong law are EXCLUDED

Functionality: F37 Central limit theorem - numeric approximation
Recognition clues: 'using the CLT, the probability … is approximately'; large n; Φ values supplied
Required output: A number obtained from Φ(b) - Φ(a)
Main method: Standardise: (S_n - nμ)/(σ√n); read Φ from the table
Common traps: Standardising with σ instead of σ√n; forgetting the continuity correction is not required here; using the CLT on a sum whose variance you computed wrongly
Exam sources: 2021spB Q6b,c; 2021spA Q3 (goal difference over 300 matches); 2019spB Q4; 2018wA Q9; 2018wB Q2; 8598-sol Q10

Functionality: F38 Check whether a proposed object is a valid distribution
Recognition clues: 'is f a density?'; a candidate PMF with a parameter
Required output: Yes/no with the failing axiom identified
Main method: Non-negativity + total mass 1 (+ σ-additivity for measures)
Common traps: Checking only the integral and not non-negativity; not checking the support
Exam sources: Used implicitly as a self-check throughout; explicitly in Raviv §1.1 examples

Functionality: F39 Self-referential / recursive probability equations
Recognition clues: A game that returns to its initial state; 'in any other case, continue to another round'
Required output: An equation P(A)=…+c·P(A) solved for P(A)
Main method: Condition on the first round; identify the state that reproduces the original problem
Common traps: Not noticing the recursion and summing an infinite series unnecessarily; forgetting the 'no winner' absorbing case
Exam sources: 2023spA Q1e (P(A) = 1/8·P(A) + … ⇒ 5/7 - the cleanest example in the folder); 2019spB Q3 (clown on a ladder)

Functionality: F40 Recurrence relations for moments (integration by parts)
Recognition clues: 'express E(Z^n) via E(Z^{n-2})'; hint 'integration by parts'
Required output: A recursion plus an explicit closed form (double factorial)
Main method: u = z^{n-1}, v' = z φ(z); boundary terms vanish
Common traps: Losing the boundary term; not treating odd n separately (it is 0 by symmetry); forgetting E|Z|^n differs from E Z^n
Exam sources: 2024wA Q2a-d (the full development: odd moments 0 by symmetry, E Z⁴=3, the recursion, and E|Z|^n)
Revision note: Direct integration by parts on the normal density. Does NOT use MGFs, so unaffected by the exclusion

Functionality: F41 Odd/even symmetry to kill an integral
Recognition clues: E(g(Z)) where g is odd and the density is even
Required output: '= 0, because the integrand is odd and the integral converges'
Main method: State that f_Z is even, z^k f_Z is odd, and the integral is finite
Common traps: Claiming 0 without checking that the integral converges (Louidor's solution explicitly says 'since the integral exists and is finite')
Exam sources: 2024wA Q2a ('רמז: ניתן לפתור באופן מיידי')

Functionality: F42 Reuse an earlier subpart's result
Recognition clues: 'you may use the final answer of one subpart in another, even if you did not solve it'
Required output: An explicit citation: 'by (ד)…'
Main method: Scan the whole question before starting; look for the quantity the next part needs
Common traps: Re-deriving from scratch and running out of time; using a result you mis-derived without sanity-checking it
Exam sources: Stated verbatim in the instructions of 2024wA (rule 6), 2024wB, 2023spA, 2023spB. Used in 2024wA Q2e (needs E|Z|^n from Q2d); 2023spA Q2e (needs Var from Q2c); 2024wB Q3e (needs Q3b)

Functionality: F43 Multinomial distribution and its conditional structure
Recognition clues: One trial with more than two outcomes, repeated
Required output: Multi(n, p_1,…,p_k); marginals are binomial
Main method: Recognise the multinomial; condition on the total when the total is random
Common traps: Assuming multinomial counts are independent (they are NOT, unless the total is Poisson)
Exam sources: 2021spB Q4 ('דרך ב'' works via Multi conditioned on N); 2018wA Q(multinomial); 2019spB Q9
Revision note: DOWNGRADED from High: its main exam role was as the fallback route inside Poisson-splitting questions, which are now excluded

Functionality: F44 Geometric-sum / infinite-series manipulation inside a probability
Recognition clues: An answer that is an infinite sum over rounds/trials
Required output: A closed form
Main method: Σ r^k = 1/(1-r); differentiate/integrate a geometric series when k appears
Common traps: Off-by-one in the starting index; forgetting |r|<1
Current-course sources: T3; Raviv §1.3.1 example (Nofar's raffle, uses ∫Σ t^n dt = ln 2)

Functionality: F45 Level of justification expected
Recognition clues: Every open question
Required output: Each step named: 'by the tower law', 'from independence', 'by Chebyshev'
Main method: Name the theorem before using it; state assumptions used
Common traps: Writing only algebra; not simplifying (2023spB rule 12 warns that unsimplified expressions lose points)
Current-course sources: Raviv's lecture proofs model the expected style
Exam sources: 2024wA rule 7; 2023spB rule 12 ('אלא אם נאמר אחרת, יש לפשט ביטויים ולפתור סכומים ואינטגרלים')

Functionality: F46 Give the distribution in ANY equivalent form
Recognition clues: 'when asked to find the distribution of an RV…'
Required output: PMF, density, CDF, MGF, or the name+parameters - all accepted
Main method: Pick the cheapest representation
Common traps: Grinding out a density when naming the distribution would have sufficed
Exam sources: Stated verbatim as rule 10 in 2024wA and rule 11 in 2023spB
Revision note: A distribution may still be given as a PMF, density, CDF, or name+parameters. The MGF option is no longer available

Functionality: F47 Complete the square inside a normal integral
Recognition clues: An integral of the form exp(-(ax^2+bx+c)/2) arising from a marginal or a conditional density of a normal-on-normal model
Required output: A recognisable normal density, so the remaining integral equals 1 and only the prefactor survives
Main method: Rewrite the exponent as -(x-m)^2/(2s^2) + constant; pull the constant out; the rest integrates to 1
Common traps: Arithmetic slips in the completion; forgetting the Jacobian-like constant when the coefficient of x^2 is not 1; not recognising the leftover prefactor as the answer's density
Exam sources: 2023spB Q4b (marginal of Y1 comes out N(0,2)); 2023spB Q4c (conditional of X given Y1 comes out N(y/2, 1/2))
Revision note: NEW: this is the load-bearing technique of the replacement Core question and was not isolated in the pre-announcement inventory

Functionality: F48 Conditional independence given a latent variable
Recognition clues: Several observations that are independent GIVEN an unobserved parameter, but dependent unconditionally; 'independently of the other bolts the machine produced'
Required output: A statement of the form E(Y2 | Y1=y, X=x) = E(Y2 | X=x), then smoothing over the posterior of X
Main method: Condition on the latent variable to restore independence, then apply the conditional smoothing formula
Common traps: Treating the observations as unconditionally independent; forgetting that the second smoothing step averages over the POSTERIOR of X, not its prior
Exam sources: 2023spB Q4e (E(Y2|Y1=y) = E(X|Y1=y) = y/2, proved via conditional independence)
